disclaimer: This guide is for career planning, not a guarantee of eligibility or selection. Post names, accepted degrees, minimum marks, age limits, exam patterns and deadlines can change between recruitment cycles. Always follow the latest official advertisement for the exact vacancy. ISRO does not require candidates to pay agents for appointment.

sc.title: Scientist/Engineer 'SC' (engineering graduates)
points: Depending on the recruitment advertisement, selection may be through a written/computer-based test and interview, through GATE-score-based shortlisting and interview, or another method stated in that notice.
Some recruitment drives combine different routes for different vacancies. Do not assume GATE is compulsory for every Scientist/Engineer post, and do not assume GATE alone guarantees selection.
Prepare the core subjects for your engineering branch, engineering mathematics where relevant, and previous papers for the exact post/discipline.
The official ICRB advertisement is the authority for accepted degrees, minimum marks, age, selection stages and dates.

gate.title: GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering)
points: Useful for engineering and some science-related recruitment routes when the specific ISRO notice accepts a GATE score.
Choose the GATE paper that matches your discipline and the advertisement's requirements.
Preparation: core undergraduate subjects, engineering mathematics where applicable, previous GATE papers, timed mock tests and error analysis.
Check the current year's official GATE website for the relevant cycle.

research.title: Research fellowships and project posts (JRF, SRF, Research Associate, Project Scientist)
points: JRF, SRF, Research Associate and Project Scientist vacancies are advertised by centres such as SAC, NRSC, PRL, URSC and others.
The criteria vary: some may ask for a relevant M.Sc./M.Tech, GATE, UGC-CSIR NET, another national test, research experience or an interview. Read the individual notice.
For Physics, Mathematics and related research pathways, UGC-CSIR NET or GATE may be relevant to certain posts, but neither is a universal requirement for all ISRO research roles.

technical.title: Technical Assistant, Technician and other support roles
points: These roles generally have their own centre-specific recruitment notification and may use a written/computer-based test, trade/skill test or other prescribed assessment.
Technical Assistant posts commonly require a relevant diploma; Technician-B commonly requires the specified ITI/trade qualification. The exact trade and marks requirements matter.
Practise the technical syllabus, trade fundamentals, mathematics/reasoning if included, and the centre's official previous papers.

admin.title: Administrative, stenography, accounts and medical roles
points: Selection may include a computer-based/written examination, skill or typing test, interview, professional assessment or document verification, depending on the post.
Medical roles require the professional qualification and registration listed in the advertisement; administrative and finance roles have their own qualification rules.

noSingleExam: There is no one common ISRO entrance exam for all jobs. ISRO's Centralised Recruitment Board (ICRB) and individual centres advertise different positions and may use different selection methods.

all.topics: Mathematics and core subjects required by the specific branch; use your university's standard textbooks and official syllabus.

mech.topics: Engineering mechanics, strength of materials, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, propulsion-related basics, control and structures as applicable.

ece.topics: Network theory, analog/digital electronics, signals and systems, communication, control systems, electromagnetic fields and microprocessors as applicable.

cs.topics: Programming, data structures and algorithms, discrete mathematics, operating systems, databases, computer networks, software engineering and theory of computation as applicable.

physics.topics: Classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, mathematical methods and the specialised subject listed for the exam.

rs.topics: Remote sensing fundamentals, GIS, coordinate systems, image processing, geospatial analysis and interpretation of satellite data.

tech.topics: Trade theory, workshop practice, safety, tools, measurements and the exact technical syllabus for the trade.

bookNote: Book selection note (from the guide): use the books prescribed by your degree programme and standard references for your branch. The official syllabus and past papers should decide what to prioritise; avoid buying large sets of books before identifying the target exam.

prepSteps: Choose one target post and read its latest official advertisement from beginning to end.
Confirm that your degree, branch, marks, age and any required experience match the eligibility criteria.
Download the syllabus and official previous papers for that post/discipline.
Build strong fundamentals in your degree subjects; practise numerical and conceptual questions rather than memorising solutions.
Take timed mock tests and keep an error notebook with topics to revise.
Prepare for the interview or skill test only if that stage is part of the stated selection process.
Apply only through official recruitment links and beware of fake appointment letters or agents asking for money.

plan.focus: Review mathematics and fundamentals of the chosen discipline; read the target recruitment syllabus.
Cover the first major core subjects and practise topic-wise questions.
Continue core subjects and work through numerical and conceptual problems.
Finish high-priority topics and begin solving previous recruitment papers.
Take timed mock tests; analyse mistakes and revise weak areas.
Practise full papers, revise formulas and confirm the latest recruitment eligibility and selection method.

dailyRoutine: Suggested daily routine: 1 to 2 hours of core subjects, 30 minutes of problem-solving and 15 minutes reviewing mistakes. Adapt this to your semester schedule and exam date.
checklist: Current education: Class 10/12, diploma/ITI, B.E./B.Tech, B.Sc./M.Sc. or graduate.
Branch or subject: CSE/IT, ECE, Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Physics, Mathematics, Geography, etc.
Preferred role: software/AI, rockets, satellite electronics, space science, remote sensing, technical work or administration.
Target qualification and eligibility: confirm in the current vacancy advertisement.
Exam route: GATE, ISRO written/CBT, interview, skill test, NET or other route only when specified.
Resources: official syllabus, previous papers, core textbooks and free NPTEL/IIRS courses where relevant.
